name: Cascader
intent: Pick one item from options that nest several levels deep by walking columns left to right, like a field on a related object (Invoice / Account / Owner) or a region / country / city.
usage: Use Cascader when the choice sits at the end of a path and people need to see each level: fields on related records, categories, locations. It is one component: pass options, each with a value, a label and, when it opens another level, children. variant field is a form field that opens the columns in a dropdown and shows the picked path (Invoice / Account / Owner); variant panel draws the columns inline, like the field picker in a modal, with the page showing the choice. Each row can carry a path in brackets (the related object or id), a type badge (Text, Num, Date) and a relation mark: parent ([+], opens the related record's fields) or children (», opens related child records). A legend under the columns explains the marks when any row has one. Only the last level can be picked unless changeOnSelect lets any level be the answer. searchable adds a search box that lists every matching path. See contracts/cascader.json for the full contract. A portaled panel takes the theme of whatever opened it, so it is dark with a dark app frame even though it is drawn at the end of the page. A label set at the start goes back on top of the field when the box around it is narrower than 480px, since a 160px label column would leave too little of the field to type in.

label.note: Field label (field) or the name of the columns for screen readers (panel).

options.itemShape: { value: string; label: string; path?: string; type?: string; relation?: "parent" | "children"; disabled?: boolean; children?: CascaderOption[] }
options.note: The first column. path shows in brackets after the label, like (Payment.Id). type is a short badge, like Text or Num. relation marks rows that open a related record: parent [+] or children ». An option with children opens a column to its right. Values are unique among siblings.

value.note: Controlled picked path: one value per level, like ["invoice", "account", "owner"].

defaultValue.note: Starting path when the Cascader keeps it itself.

onChange.note: Called with the picked path and its options.

variant.note: field: a form field with the columns in a dropdown. panel: the columns inline, with a border, for a modal or a side panel.

changeOnSelect.note: Any level can be picked, not only the last. Clicking a row with children both picks it and opens its column.

searchable.note: A search box over the columns. Typing lists every path whose labels match; picking one sets the whole path.

showLegend.note: The legend bar under the columns, explaining the relation marks. Shows only when some option has a relation.

placeholder.note: For field, when nothing is picked.

size.note: Field height, like Select. md when not set; a surrounding Density changes it through the density tokens. Columns keep 28 rows.

labelPosition.note: For field, like Select. Follows Form.

name.note: Adds a hidden input with the path joined by dots, for forms.

help.note: Opens a HelpPopover from a help icon next to the label, like other fields.

emptyLabel.note: Shown when a search finds nothing.

useWhen: The answer sits at the end of a path of two or more levels, like a field on a related record.
People need to see which level each choice lives on while they browse.
A field picker in a modal or side panel, with variant panel.
doNot: Do not use it for a flat list. Use Select.
Do not use it to browse or arrange a hierarchy without picking. Use TreeView.
Do not nest Selects to fake levels, or build local columns. Use Cascader.
a11y: Each column is a listbox named by label and its level; rows are options. The rows on the open path are selected.

One row is in the tab order. Up and Down move in a column, Home and End go to its ends; Right (or Enter) opens a row's column and moves into it; Left goes back to the parent row; Enter or Space picks a row that can be picked.
field: the field is a button with aria-expanded; the dropdown opens on click, Enter, Space or Down, and Escape or a click outside closes it and gives focus back.
Relation marks are icons with names (Related parent, Related children), explained by the legend. Type badges are kit Badges.
The newest column scrolls into view when it opens.

examples.title: Field
examples.usage: A form field that opens the columns in a dropdown and shows the picked path.

examples.title: Panel
examples.usage: Columns inline, like the field picker in a modal: types, related records and the legend.

examples.title: Any level
examples.usage: With changeOnSelect, a related record itself can be the answer, not only its fields.
